properties.name: get_skill serves the skill a slash command names, instead of refusing with the mapping
properties.rationale:
Measured on flo2's connector, 2026-09-24 (flo2 fact:first-skill-runs-through-the-doors-2026-09-24): a chat model asked get_skill for "gaps", was refused, read the mapping in the refusal, and asked again for "detect-and-ask".

The refusal (chg:accept-e5fb205599c26447, 2026-08-19) was the right fix for its time, when a caller got a bare list. But a slash command that names a skill has exactly one answer. Refusing it and naming that answer costs every caller a round trip and teaches nothing the reply's `requested_as` cannot.

flo2 resolves shortcuts in its own gateway meanwhile. This makes every client right, including Claude Code users who type a command's word.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
get_skill now accepts the word a person types, and serves that skill. "gaps", "/gaps", "/where" and "/impact-check" each work, and a skill's own name works with or without a slash (skills::resolve).
- The reply carries `requested_as` when what was asked for is not the skill's name.
- A command that is a TOOL rather than a skill (/debt, /decisions, /next) still refuses and names the tool.
- The tool description, the `name` argument's description, the get_skill toolsnap and docs/skills-and-tools.md are updated to match.
- Tests: `asking_by_the_typed_name_serves_the_skill` replaces the refusal test, plus `a_command_that_is_a_tool_refuses_and_names_the_tool`, `a_skill_by_its_own_name_says_nothing_extra`, and a unit test `a_slash_command_resolves_to_the_skill_it_names`.
